For real normal M, polar M=QH, T=p(eta M), W_n=Σ(T^k)^T T^k commute; each scalar covariance between xi_j and Q^T zeta_j is <=sigma^2, equality forces coordinate equality a.s., so unique coupling zeta=Qxi even among non-Gaussian joints. Spectral weights give exact n and stationary contraction formulas. Zero stationary noise requires eta H=I, hence M=rQ. For orthogonal mode e^{iθ} with cosθ>0, |p(e^{iθ})|=|2cosθ-1|<1 iff cosθ<1; an odd real orthogonal matrix must have +1 or -1, monotonicity excludes -1; rotations supply all even dimensions. Conditional unbiasedness E[zeta|xi]=0 eliminates cross term. Independent 3 direct computations corroborated the analytical argument.
